neighbours.label: a superlative that identifies a place or group by rank instead of naming it (the most populous Arab country, the world's largest democracy), peaking on the superlative, as opposed to the name itself or a description without rank
fire: Elections are coming soon in the most populous state of Germany.
Storms hit the country's largest port on Monday night.
Reporters flew to the smallest republic in South America.
Food prices rose sharply across the most populous nation in Africa.
The president visited the world's second-largest economy last spring.
New roads will connect the region's largest city to the coast.
Pilgrims travel each year to the world's largest Muslim country.
Doctors are scarce in the least populated province of Canada.
quiet: Elections are coming soon in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Storms hit Rotterdam and its docks on Monday night.
Reporters flew to Suriname to cover the vote.
Food prices rose sharply across Nigeria and its neighbors.
The president visited an oil-rich nation last spring.
New roads will connect a busy river town to the coast.
Pilgrims travel each year to Indonesia and its islands.
Doctors are scarce in a remote mountain province of Canada.

short: ranking a place instead of naming it
notes: Card: ' populous' x2, ' last' x3, ' first' x2, ' third' x2, ' of' x5; the - pole is ' other', ' one', ' third', the determiner reading of these words. Probes: most populous 0.40-0.55, largest island 0.39, largest democracy 0.38, smallest state 0.23, second-largest 0.24; named places 0.01-0.05, oil-rich kingdom 0.04. Ordinals also fired ('turn of the last century' 0.48, 'first book of the Torah' 0.47, 'first book on the shelf' 0.03), which this test does not cover.
